passages.happening:
God tells Ezekiel to set his face against Mount Seir and prophesy against it. God will make it a desolate waste (verses 2-4). ‘Because you harbored an ancient hatred and delivered the Israelites over to the sword in the time of their disaster’ (verse 5), bloodshed will pursue Edom (verse 6).

Edom said, ‘These two nations and countries will be ours, and we will possess them,’ ‘even though the LORD was there’ (verse 10). God has heard every contemptuous word Edom spoke against the mountains of Israel, saying they were desolate and given to it to devour (verse 12). ‘As you rejoiced when the inheritance of the house of Israel became desolate, so will I do to you’ (verse 15).
passages.hearers:
Edom lay south and southeast of the Dead Sea, in the rugged highlands called Seir. Israel traced the Edomites to Esau, Jacob's brother, so the hatred is a family feud centuries old. When Babylon destroyed Jerusalem, Edom sided with the conqueror and took advantage of Judah's collapse. Psalm 137, Obadiah and Lamentations all remember it bitterly. Letters from the Judean fortress of Arad, from Judah's last years, show worry about an Edomite threat in the south.

The two nations are Israel and Judah. With both emptied of their people, Edom assumed the land was free for the taking. The phrase, even though the LORD was there, is the heart of it: the land was never empty, because God had not given it up.

Addressing Mount Seir prepares for the next chapter, addressed to the mountains of Israel. The punishment fits the crime: Edom rejoiced over desolation, so it will become desolate.
passages.later: Obadiah said that Edom, on the day of Jerusalem's fall, was ‘just like one of them’ (Obadiah 1:11). Yet the law said, ‘Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother’ (Deuteronomy 23:7).
passages.hard:
Isn't it troubling to celebrate the destruction of a whole people, and are Edom's descendants still under this curse?

The oracle is severe, and readers should feel its weight. Several things help place it. It is a judgment on specific conduct, Edom's part in the killing and plundering of Judeans after 587 or 586 BC, not a statement about Edomites as a people by birth. Israel's own law told Israel not to despise an Edomite, because he is a brother, and the prophets could picture Edom among the nations called by God's name (Amos 9:12). The lasting desolation concerns the land and state of Edom, which in time ceased to exist as a kingdom; Edomites who moved into southern Judah were later absorbed into the Jewish people in the second century BC.

Scripture teaches no ongoing curse on any people descended from them, and no people today is a stand-in for Edom. Some readers also take Edom, here and in later Jewish writing, as a type of the hostile nations in general.
passages.asks: Edom nursed an ancient hatred until it saw its chance. Ask whether you are carrying an old grudge that waits for its moment. And ask what it would take to let God judge it instead.
